newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares again lead rise on Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares again lead rise on Beirut bourse.

text.p: Two out of three listed bank shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Tuesday and brokers said the rises were driven by high expectations for mid-year profits.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Bank of Beirut hit record highs. BLC rose to $18.25 from $17.625 and BOB reached $4 from $3.8125. Banque Audi was unchanged at $23.125, another record high.
Among the shares of the other five listed companies three were unchanged, one fell and there was no trade in two others.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.8 percent to 155.02. The LISPI general index rose 0.61 percent to 155.02 and the BLOM general index rose 0.08 percent to 943.5.
"It is an earnings expectation driven price rise," Nicholas Sawan of Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said of the bank shares.
"We are in June, coming towards half-year results. Even though banks don't do miracles, we are expecting results very close to that, very good earnings," he told Reuters.
Sawan said BLC GDRs had reached $20.5 on the London Stock Exchange and the underlying shares were likely to rise quickly to $20 in Beirut.

Another broker, who asked not to be identified, said BOB should consolidate at $4 while BLC was expected to rise to $19 before consolidating there. He said the rise in BLC GDRs followed the Beirut rise.
The three banks reported strong profits growth in the first quarter.
Solidere A and B were unchanged at $10.75 amid heavy demand.
"It is a very healthy consolidation for Solidere but trading volumes are still thin," a broker said.
Of the four industrial firms, pipemaker Eternit slipped to $2.00 from $2.03125 on turnover of 3,500 shares while Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125 on turnover of 30,000 shares.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic or Ciments Blancs.
Total BSE turnover was 213,212 shares for a value of $1,355,106 from 375,496 shares for $2,330,908 a day earlier.
